79528164.title: The Story & the Engine
79528164.extract:
"The Story & the Engine" is the fifth episode of the fifteenth series of the British science-fiction television series Doctor Who. It was written by Inua Ellams, directed by Makalla McPherson, and released on BBC iPlayer, BBC One, and Disney+ on 10 May 2025. In the episode, the Fifteenth Doctor (Ncuti Gatwa) and his companion, Belinda Chandra (Varada Sethu), visit Lagos, Nigeria. There, they get trapped in a barbershop by an enigmatic figure, known only as the Barber, who uses the power of stories to power an engine he constructed.
The episode shares a similar setting, cast, and themes to the Barber Shop Chronicles, a play written by Ellams. Featuring a largely BIPOC cast and exploring motifs of identity, it was primarily filmed at Wolf Studios Wales in Cardiff in early 2024. Some footage was recorded in Lagos, with the primary goal to make the soundstage set look authentic. The episode was viewed by 2.70 million viewers and received generally positive reviews from critics, particularly for its script.


== Plot ==
The Fifteenth Doctor and Belinda Chandra arrive in Lagos, Nigeria in 2019. Belinda remains in the TARDIS while The Doctor visits Omo, a friend who runs a barbershop. The Doctor discovers Omo and several others have gone missing, and upon entering the shop, becomes trapped inside. Omo reveals that a mysterious figure dubbed "The Barber" took control of the shop and forces the missing men to power an engine by telling stories. The Barber is working alongside a woman named Abby, who the Doctor recognises but cannot identify.
The Doctor is unhappy when he finds out that Omo told the Barber about him. The Doctor attempts to escape the barbershop but nearly falls out because the shop is traveling on a giant colossal spider walking along a massive web. The Barber explains that the shop exists both in Lagos and on the spider, and that only he and Abby are able to leave. Belinda arrives and also becomes trapped. The Doctor goads the Barber into revealing his identity: a storyteller who assisted many gods by spreading and preserving their stories using the web, which is also called the Nexus. The Nexus functioned too well, which led the gods to cut him off it. The Doctor realises that Abby is actually Abena, the daughter of Anansi, who he abandoned while in his Fugitive incarnation due to other commitments, and that Abena allied with the Barber to seek revenge.
The Barber reveals that he intends to reach the centre of the Nexus in order to cut off all the gods from the web and thus kill them, which would destabilise human culture. Abena, having a change of heart after being convinced by the others, braids the Doctor's hair into a map, guiding him to the centre of the engine's power source. The Doctor and Belinda reconfigure the heart of the engine to allow the Doctor to power it with his own life story. The energy is too much, and the engine begins to destroy itself. The Doctor persuades the Barber to release the trapped people and to escape with them. The engine is destroyed, returning the shop to normal.
The missing men all return to their loved ones, and Omo apologises and makes up with the Doctor. Omo retires and puts the Barber in charge of running the shop, while Abena goes off to live her life. The Doctor and Belinda depart as the Doctor tells her the story of how he met Omo.


== Production ==


=== Development ===
The episode was written by Inua Ellams, marking his first full contribution to Doctor Who. Ellams was originally approached by the series' previous showrunner, Chris Chibnall, to become involved with it; on the recommendation of fellow writers, Chibnall had read his and Vinay Patel's essays in The Good Immigrant, which both made mention of watching and enjoying the programme in their youth and childhoods. Whilst Patel would subsequently author one script ("Demons of the Punjab") and co-author another ("Fugitive of the Judoon") under Chibnall, Ellams' writing contributions during the earlier development of the show's shortened, COVID-19-hit thirteenth series ultimately did not extend as far as a completed episode.
Ellams aimed to write for the series again following the September 2021 announcement of Russell T Davies' return as showrunner. He first attempted to reach out to Davies through his agent, but was told he was busy with early work on devising his own stories. Ellams instead sent Davies a direct message via Instagram, to which he responded, with the two entering initial talks for him to write an episode. In addition to this, Ellams was personally recommended to Davies by series star Ncuti Gatwa, unaware that the two were already in contact. Initially, a different, "much larger" idea had been developed by Ellams, but was rejected by Davies because it was too similar to another script that was already being developed for the series. After the other writer was ultimately unable to complete their script, Davies suggested to Ellams that he write a story set in a barbershop, having previously seen his stage play Barber Shop Chronicles. According to Ellams, despite the play and the episode being independent ideas with original characters, he views them as having "connective tissue" for their underlying concepts. 
The idea for the Barber came to Ellams after he learned that the term for "ghost writer" in the French language was "le nègre" (lit. 'Black person'). He decided to expand on that concept by making the antagonist an African male who had written stories for everyone and did not receive any credit for their work. This was later connected to Anansi, a West African mythological character known for associations with stories. Ellams also wrote the episode as a "companion piece" to the 2024 Doctor Who episode "Dot and Bubble", because of how the Doctor's skin colour played into the story. According to Davies, Ellams' episode was initially intended to be sequenced directly after "Dot and Bubble" as part of the fourteenth series, but was ultimately pushed back into the fifteenth, due to the later decision to instead include a script written by Kate Herron and Briony Redman ("Rogue").
At one time, there were concerns over whether the episode's antagonist was "too frightening". However, throughout writing it, Ellams kept advice given to him by Chris Chibnall that the series is "a sci-fi and horror for eight-year-olds, but also for all ages" in mind. The episode explores themes of "identity, displacement, and destiny". Elements of two poems written by Ellams for his 2020 poetry compilation book The Actual, "Fuck / Time" and "Fuck / Drums", are repurposed in it; the former is used for the first story told about Yo-Yo Ma, and the latter references Doctor Who, mentioning the TARDIS in an expression of Afrofuturism. The episode's setting of Lagos, Nigeria, was identified by Gatwa as a "dream storyline" for him in 2022, prior to it being written.


=== Casting ===

With the exception of flashback scenes and archive footage, the episode features a cast entirely comprising people of colour. Gatwa and Varada Sethu star as the fifteenth incarnation of the Doctor and his companion, Belinda Chandra. Ariyon Bakare guest stars as "the Barber", Sule Rimi appears as Omo, the barbershop's owner, while Stefan Adegbola, Jordan Adene, and Michael Balogun portray customers. Michelle Asante portrays Abena. Bakare made his character similar to Anansi and the biblical figure Samson. Rimi and Balogun had previously worked with Ellams when they performed in his play Barber Shop Chronicles. Rimi had also appeared in Doctor Who twice before in the 2005 episode "Aliens of London" as a member of UNIT and in the 2015 story "The Magician's Apprentice" as a newsreader, while Bakare appeared as Leandro in "The Woman Who Lived" (2015).
The episode's author, Inua Ellams makes a cameo appearance in the episode, which came about after he made a joke about appearing in the episode during a meeting. Jo Martin reprises her role as the Fugitive Doctor. Showrunner Russell T Davies stated that because the episode explored the Doctor's ethnicity, it "felt like Jo Martin was missing" and that he wanted to "acknowledge her" and show that the character "still exists." Additionally, all of the past performers who regularly starred as the Doctor appear in archive footage. The remainder of the guest cast includes Adrian Pang and Anita Dobson as a consultant and Mrs Flood, respectively. Sienna-Robyn Mavanga-Phipps briefly reprises her role as Poppy from "Space Babies" (2024), with her appearance to Belinda unexplained during the episode. Eighty extras were used in the Nigerian market scene.


=== Filming ===

"The Story & the Engine" was directed by Makalla McPherson. It was filmed in early 2024 and was placed in the fourth production block of the series along with the following episode, "The Interstellar Song Contest". Although both episodes in a single block would normally be overseen by the same director, complexity of the next story required them to have individual directors. Filming on the episode coincided with Gatwa's appearance at the 96th Academy Awards for Barbie.
The production team initially considered actually filming the episode in Lagos, Nigeria, where the story is set, but found the prospect of the full cast and crew travelling there to be too expensive. Instead, a set was built on soundstage 7 at Wolf Studios Wales in Cardiff. However, establishing drone shots were still recorded in Lagos. McPherson used previsualization to see a three-dimensional virtual version of the set prior to construction, which was used to plan blocking, action sequences, and set design. She said that the main obstacle was creating a proper dynamic among the cast since the episode had a single main set.
The Nigerian market scene was filmed at Wolf Studios on 19 February 2024. Only one day of shooting was allocated to that scene before the sound stage began conversion to the exterior of the barbershop and alleyways. The back of the barbershop and engine room were constructed on a separate soundstage. Multiple Nigerian consultants were involved with various areas of production to ensure authentic representation of sets, hair styles, and spoken languages.


== Broadcast and reception ==


=== Broadcast ===
"The Story & the Engine" was simultaneously released on BBC iPlayer at 8 a.m. British Summer Time (BST) in the United Kingdom and on Disney+ in the United States at 12 a.m. Pacific Daylight Time on 10 May 2025. A BBC One broadcast of the episode followed at 7:10 p.m. BST. Disney also handled international distribution of the episode.


=== Ratings ===
The episode received overnight ratings of 1.59 million. Within seven days, the total number of viewers had risen to 2.70 million.


=== Critical reception ===
On the review aggregator website Rotten Tomatoes, 89% of 9 critics' reviews are positive. Stefan Mohamed, writing for Den of Geek, responded positively to the episode, praising the usage of the Doctor's race, Ellams's writing, the episode's settings, and the episode's unique atmosphere, but criticised the episode's overcomplicated ideas and a lack of identifiable stakes. Will Salmon from GamesRadar+ cited the episode as "one of the most original and ambitious episodes this show has produced in years", pointing out the episode's unique way of telling its story. Robert Anderson, writing for IGN, emphasised the episode's story and premise, though criticised the episode's reliance on gods, feeling it was overused due to the number of god-like entities that had appeared in recent episodes. Adi Tantimedh, writing for Bleeding Cool, praised the episode, highlighting Bakare's performance, the episode's unique presentation, and the characterization and writing of the Doctor.
Ryan Woodrow, writing for Newsweek, stated that while he enjoyed the episode's final act, he felt the episode needed a narrower focus; he believed the risks were not well-defined until halfway through the episode, which he felt would leave viewers confused, and that the men trapped in the shop "fade into the background" once danger was defined. Patrick Mulkern, writing for Radio Times, offered a negative review, criticising the episode's depiction of Nigeria, and also criticised Jo Martin’s cameo as "wasted".


== References ==


== External links ==

"The Story & the Engine" at the Doctor Who Stories Website

"The Story & the Engine" on Tardis Wiki, the Doctor Who Wiki
"The Story & the Engine" at IMDb

responded, with the two entering initial talks for him to write an episode.<ref name="Prescott-2025" /> In addition to this, Ellams was personally recommended to Davies by series star [[Ncuti Gatwa]], unaware that the two were already in contact.<ref name="DWMPreview">{{cite magazine |last=Atkinson|first=Richard|editor-last=Quinn |editor-first=Jason|title=Preview - The Story & the Engine|date=24 April 2025|magazine=[[Doctor Who Magazine]] |issue=616 |publisher=[[Panini Comics|Panini Magazines]] |pages=16–18}}</ref><ref name="Episode BTS">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=g27KPGp-_LY |title=Delving into the Doctor's Past {{!}} Behind the Scenes of The Story & the Engine {{!}} Doctor Who |date=10 May 2025 |access-date=10 May 2025 |via=[[YouTube]] |type=Behind the scenes featurette |archive-date=10 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250510195130/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=g27KPGp-_LY |url-status=live }}</ref> Initially, a different, "much larger" idea had been developed by Ellams,<ref name="www.doctorwho.tv">{{Cite web |title=‘The Story & the Engine’ writer Inua Ellams on bringing West African folklore to Doctor Who {{!}} Doctor Who |url=https://www.doctorwho.tv/news-and-features/the-story-the-engine-writer-inua-ellams-on-bringing-west-african-folklore-to |archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20250618091842/https://www.doctorwho.tv/news-and-features/the-story-the-engine-writer-inua-ellams-on-bringing-west-african-folklore-to |archive-date=2025-06-18 |access-date=2025-09-16 |website=www.doctorwho.tv |language=en}}</ref> but was rejected by Davies because it was too similar to another script that was already being developed for the series.<ref name="Prescott-2025" /> After the other writer was ultimately unable to complete their script, Davies suggested to Ellams that he write a story set in a barbershop, having previously seen his [[stage play]] ''Barber Shop Chronicles''.<ref name="Prescott-2025">{{cite web|url=https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/doctor-who-writer-teases-episode-five-barbershop-safe-place/|title=Doctor Who Writer Teases Episode Five: "The Barbershop is a Safe Place To Be…"|last=Prescott|first=Amanda-Rae|date=8 May 2025|accessdate=16 May 2025|work=[[Den of Geek]]|archive-date=10 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250510055353/https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/doctor-who-writer-teases-episode-five-barbershop-safe-place/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Peter-2025">{{Cite web |last=Peter |first=Dennis Ade |date=2025-05-16 |title=How Inua Ellams Brought African Folklore and Poetry into the ‘Doctor Who’ Universe {{!}} OkayAfrica |url=https://www.okayafrica.com/how-inua-ellams-brought-african-folklore-and-poetry-into-the-doctor-who-universe/200708 |access-date=2025-09-15 |website=www.okayafrica.com |language=en-US}}</ref> According to Ellams, despite the play and the episode being independent ideas with original characters, he views them as having "connective tissue" for their underlying concepts.<ref name="DWMPreview" /><ref name="Episode BTS" /> 

The idea for the Barber came to Ellams after he learned that the term for "[[ghostwriter|ghost writer]]" in the [[French language]] was "[[wikt:nègre|le nègre]]" ({{literal translation|Black person}}).<ref name="Den of Geek Ellams" /> He decided to expand on that concept by making the antagonist an African male who had written stories for everyone and did not receive any credit for their work. This was later connected to [[Anansi]], a [[West African mythology|West African mythological]] character known for associations with stories.<ref name="Den of Geek Ellams">{{cite web|url=https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/doctor-who-writer-explains-the-story-amp-the-engine-inspirations-ending/|title=Doctor Who Writer Explains "The Story & The Engine" Inspirations and Ending|last=Prescott|first=Amanda-Rae|date=10 May 2025|accessdate=16 May 2025|work=[[Den of Geek]]|archive-date=14 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250514154319/https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/doctor-who-writer-explains-the-story-amp-the-engine-inspirations-ending/|url-status=live}}</ref> Ellams also wrote the episode as a "companion piece" to the 2024 ''Doctor Who'' episode "[[Dot and Bubble]]", because of how the Doctor's skin colour played into the story.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-dot-bubble-companion-piece-exclusive-newsupdate/|title=Doctor Who writer reveals why next episode is a companion piece to Dot and Bubble|last=Hewitt|first=Jack|date=6 May 2025|accessdate=11 May 2025|work=[[Radio Times]]|archive-date=10 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250510201510/https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-dot-bubble-companion-piece-exclusive-newsupdate/|url-status=live}}</ref> According to Davies, Ellams' episode was initially intended to be sequenced directly after "Dot and Bubble" as part of [[Doctor Who series 14|the fourteenth series]], but was ultimately pushed back into [[Doctor Who series 15|the fifteenth]], due to the later decision to instead include a script written by [[Kate Herron]] and Briony Redman ("[[Rogue (Doctor Who)|Rogue]]").<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Davies |first=Russell T |date=15 June 2025 |title=Production Notes | issue=617 |magazine=Doctor Who Magazine |location=United Kingdom |publisher=Panini }}</ref>

At one time, there were concerns over whether the episode's antagonist was "too frightening".<ref name="Antagonist">{{cite web|url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-story-engine-villain-barber-exclusive-newsupdate/|title=Doctor Who's new villain sparked concern over being too frightening|last=Griffin|first=Louise|date=10 May 2025|accessdate=11 May 2025|work=[[Radio Times]]|archive-date=10 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250510232959/https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-story-engine-villain-barber-exclusive-newsupdate/|url-status=live}}</ref> However, throughout writing it, Ellams kept advice given to him by Chris Chibnall that the series is "a sci-fi and horror for eight-year-olds, but also for all ages" in mind.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hibbs |first=James |title=Doctor Who writer reveals advice from former showrunner Chris Chibnall {{!}} Radio Times |url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-writer-chibnall-advice-newsupdate/ |access-date=2025-09-16 |website=www.radiotimes.com |language=en-GB}}</ref> The episode explores themes of "identity, displacement, and destiny".<ref name="DWMPreview" /> Elements of two poems written by Ellams for his 2020 poetry compilation book ''The Actual'', "Fuck / Time" and "Fuck / Drums", are repurposed in it; the former is used for the first story told about [[Yo-Yo Ma]], and the latter references ''Doctor Who'', mentioning the [[TARDIS]] in an expression of [[Afrofuturism]].<ref name="Peter-2025" /><ref name="www.doctorwho.tv" /> The episode's setting of [[Lagos, Nigeria]], was identified by Gatwa as a "dream storyline" for him in 2022, prior to it being written.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Molina-Whyte |first=Lidia |title=Ncuti Gatwa reveals his dream Doctor Who storyline {{!}} Radio Times |url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-ncuti-gatwa-storyline-newsupdate/ |access-date=2025-09-18 |website=www.radiotimes.com |language=en-GB}}</ref>

With the exception of flashback scenes and archive footage, the episode features a cast entirely comprising [[people of colour]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mashable.com/article/doctor-who-story-engine|title='Doctor Who' just did its first full-on African episode, and it's amazing|last=Taylor|first=Chris|date=10 May 2025|accessdate=10 May 2025|work=[[Mashable]]|archive-date=10 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250510070837/https://mashable.com/article/doctor-who-story-engine|url-status=live}}</ref> Gatwa and [[Varada Sethu]] star as the [[Fifteenth Doctor|fifteenth incarnation]] of [[the Doctor]] and his [[Companion (Doctor Who)|companion]], [[Belinda Chandra]]. [[Ariyon Bakare]] guest stars as "the Barber", Sule Rimi appears as Omo, the barbershop's owner, while Stefan Adegbola, Jordan Adene, and Michael Balogun portray customers. Michelle Asante portrays Abena.<ref name="Cast">{{cite web|url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-story-and-engine-cast/|title=Doctor Who: The Story and the Engine cast|last=Hibbs|first=James|date=10 May 2025|accessdate=11 May 2025|work=[[Radio Times]]|archive-date=11 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250511032831/https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-story-and-engine-cast/|url-status=live}}</ref> Bakare made his character similar to [[Anansi]] and the biblical figure [[Samson]].<ref name="Antagonist" /> Rimi and Balogun had previously worked with Ellams when they performed in his play ''Barber Shop Chronicles''.<ref name="DWMPreview" /> Rimi had also appeared in ''Doctor Who'' twice before in the 2005 episode "[[Aliens of London]]" as a member of [[UNIT]] and in the 2015 story "[[The Magician's Apprentice (Doctor Who)|The Magician's Apprentice]]" as a newsreader, while Bakare appeared as Leandro in "[[The Woman Who Lived]]" (2015).<ref name="Unleashed">{{cite episode |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/iplayer/episode/m002c5gy |title=The Story & the Engine |series=Doctor Who: Unleashed |series-link=Doctor Who: Unleashed |series-no=15 |number=5 |credits=Powell, Steffan (presenter); Aiken, Jonathon (director) |network=[[BBC]] |station=[[BBC Three]] and [[BBC iPlayer]] |airdate=10 May 2025 |access-date=11 May 2025}}</ref><ref name="DWMFollow" />

=== Filming ===
[[File:Mushin Market, Lagos.jpg|thumb|right|[[Establishing shot]]s were recorded with a drone in [[Lagos, Nigeria]].|alt=Aerial photograph of a market in Nigeria]]
"The Story & the Engine" was directed by Makalla McPherson.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/doctor-who-series-15-episode-titles/ |title=Doctor Who Series 15 Episode Titles Tease "Planet Belinda" Mystery |last=Mellor |first=Louisa |date=24 March 2025 |access-date=10 May 2025 |work=[[Den of Geek]] |archive-date=7 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250407093615/https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/doctor-who-series-15-episode-titles/ |url-status=live }}</ref> It was filmed in early 2024 and was placed in the fourth production block of the series along with the following episode, "[[The Interstellar Song Contest]]". Although both episodes in a single block would normally be overseen by the same director, complexity of the next story required them to have individual directors. Filming on the episode coincided with Gatwa's appearance at the [[96th Academy Awards]] for ''[[Barbie (film)|Barbie]]''.<ref name="DWMFollow">{{cite magazine|title=A Cut Above the Rest", "Another Story", and "Douze Points|magazine=[[Doctor Who Magazine]]|issue=617|pages=27–31|editor-last=Quinn|editor-first=Joseph|date=22 May 2025|page= |publisher=[[Panini Comics|Panini Magazines]]}}</ref>

The production team initially considered actually filming the episode in [[Lagos, Nigeria]], where the story is set, but found the prospect of the full cast and crew travelling there to be too expensive. Instead, a set was built on [[soundstage]] 7 at [[Wolf Studios Wales]] in [[Cardiff]].<ref name="Bad Wolf Access All Areas">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9-NNDFnHfOM |title=Access All Areas: Bad Wolf Studio Tour with Varada Sethu |date=26 May 2025 |access-date=26 May 2025 |via=[[YouTube]] |type=Behind the scenes featurette}}</ref> However, [[Establishing shot|establishing drone shots]] were still recorded in Lagos.<ref name="Unleashed" /> McPherson used [[previsualization]] to see a three-dimensional virtual version of the set prior to construction, which was used to plan [[Blocking (stage)|blocking]], action sequences, and set design. She said that the main obstacle was creating a proper dynamic among the cast since the episode had a single main set.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.doctorwho.tv/news-and-features/doctor-who-is-full-of-incredible-stories-and-this-is-what-happens-in-barber-shops|title="Doctor Who is full of incredible stories, and this is what happens in barber shops" – What to expect from the next exciting episode|date=8 May 2025|work=DoctorWhoTV}}</ref>

The Nigerian market scene was filmed at Wolf Studios on 19 February 2024. Only one day of shooting was allocated to that scene before the sound stage began conversion to the exterior of the barbershop and alleyways.<ref name="Unleashed" /> The back of the barbershop and engine room were constructed on a separate soundstage.<ref name="Episode BTS" /> Multiple Nigerian consultants were involved with various areas of production to ensure authentic representation of sets, hair styles, and [[Languages of Nigeria|spoken languages]].<ref name="Unleashed" /><ref name="DWMPreview" />

Release Schedule |last=Cremona |first=Patrick |date=3 May 2025 |access-date=10 May 2025 |work=[[Radio Times]] |archive-date=11 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250411210917/https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-times-release-schedule/ |url-status=live }}</ref> A [[BBC One]] broadcast of the episode followed at 7:10 p.m. BST.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.techradar.com/streaming/disney-plus/what-is-the-release-date-and-time-for-doctor-who-season-2-episode-5-on-disney-and-bbc-one|title=What is the release date and time for Doctor Who season 2 episode 5 on Disney+ and BBC One?|last=Power|first=Tom|date=8 May 2025|accessdate=10 May 2025|work=[[Tech Radar]]|archive-date=8 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250508164403/https://www.techradar.com/streaming/disney-plus/what-is-the-release-date-and-time-for-doctor-who-season-2-episode-5-on-disney-and-bbc-one|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Disney]] also handled international distribution of the episode.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cinemablend.com/streaming-news/how-to-watch-doctor-who-season-15-free |title=How To Watch Doctor Who Season 15 Online And Stream Every Episode For Free From Anywhere |last=Pateman |first=Daniel |date=12 April 2025 |access-date=10 May 2025 |work=[[Cinema Blend]] |archive-date=23 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250423080804/https://www.cinemablend.com/streaming-news/how-to-watch-doctor-who-season-15-free |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Critical reception ===
{{Rotten Tomatoes prose|89|3=9}}<ref name="RT" /> Stefan Mohamed, writing for ''[[Den of Geek]]'', responded positively to the episode, praising the usage of the Doctor's race, Ellams's writing, the episode's settings, and the episode's unique atmosphere, but criticised the episode's overcomplicated ideas and a lack of identifiable stakes.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/doctor-who-series-15-episode-5-review-the-story-the-engine/|title=Doctor Who Series 15 Episode 5 Review: The Story & The Engine|last=Mohamed|first=Stefan|date=10 May 2025|accessdate=10 May 2025|work=[[Den of Geek]]|archive-date=10 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250510083740/https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/doctor-who-series-15-episode-5-review-the-story-the-engine/|url-status=live}}</ref> Will Salmon from ''[[GamesRadar+]]'' cited the episode as "one of the most original and ambitious episodes this show has produced in years", pointing out the episode's unique way of telling its story.<ref name="GR+" /> Robert Anderson, writing for ''[[IGN]]'', emphasised the episode's story and premise, though criticised the episode's reliance on gods, feeling it was overused due to the number of god-like entities that had appeared in recent episodes.<ref name="IGN" /> Adi Tantimedh, writing for ''[[Bleeding Cool]]'', praised the episode, highlighting Bakare's performance, the episode's unique presentation, and the characterization and writing of the Doctor.<ref name="BC" />

Ryan Woodrow, writing for ''[[Newsweek]]'', stated that while he enjoyed the episode's final act, he felt the episode needed a narrower focus; he believed the risks were not well-defined until halfway through the episode, which he felt would leave viewers confused, and that the men trapped in the shop "fade into the background" once danger was defined.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Woodrow |first=Ryan |date=2025-05-10 |title=Review: Doctor Who The Story & The Engine has a messy start but a good end |url=https://www.newsweek.com/entertainment/tv/review-doctor-who-story-engine-tells-messy-tale-good-ending-2070253 |access-date=2025-05-10 |website=Newsweek |language=en |archive-date=10 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250510081308/https://www.newsweek.com/entertainment/tv/review-doctor-who-story-engine-tells-messy-tale-good-ending-2070253 |url-status=live }}</ref> Patrick Mulkern, writing for ''[[Radio Times]]'', offered a negative review, criticising the episode's depiction of Nigeria, and also criticised Jo Martin’s cameo as "wasted".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-the-story-and-the-engine/|title=Doctor Who: The Story & the Engine|last=Mulkern|first=Patrick|date=10 May 2025|accessdate=16 May 2025|work=[[Radio Times]]|archive-date=15 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250515051146/https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-the-story-and-the-engine/|url-status=live}}</ref>
